raised.claim: The model-authored `issue.body` is placed before the rendered scope block, and `parseScopeBlock` takes the first match, so a body containing its own ```triage-scope fence overrides the real scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the model puts a ```triage-scope fenced block with valid JSON in the new issue body, `BLOCK_RE` matches that one first. The issue then silently carries a scope the plan guards never validated, for example one that bypasses `isLegalScope`. This is the same hijack class the PR fixed for `contains` values, but through the free-text body.

raised.claim: The saturation check uses a count snapshotted before the run and ignores rows already attached to the same issue earlier in this plan.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an issue has 11 post-creation rows and one batch of up to 50 verdicts targets it, every verdict passes the `>= 12` check because the count stays at 11. The issue can then receive many more rows in a single run and overshoot the cap.

raised.quote:
if (!allowedKeys.has(verdict.new_issue_key!)) { skipped++; continue; }
      pushInto(byKey, verdict.new_issue_key!, verdict);
raised.claim: Verdicts routed to a new issue are never checked against that issue's own proposed scope, so the scope-contradiction guard is bypassed on this path.
raised.why_it_breaks: A new_issue with scope `{where:[candidates_count > 0]}` and a verdict for a row with `candidates_count = 0` is accepted and filed. The issue is born with a row that contradicts its own scope, which is the exact misroute guard 2 is meant to stop.

raised.claim: The strict scope schema is embedded in AnalysisSchema, so one malformed scope term (unknown col, `null` value on a numeric or `contains` op) fails parsing of the entire analysis.
raised.why_it_breaks: The tool schema types `col`, `op` and `value` loosely (`value: string|number|null`), so the model can emit a term zod rejects, such as `contains` with value null. The whole response then fails to parse and all verdicts for the day are lost, instead of dropping only the bad new_issue.
